passage:
Workers replacing water pipes found old wooden pipes under a street. Students were invited to see them before they were removed.
The engineer explained that earlier cities used different materials and methods to move water. The wooden pipes seemed strange, but they had worked for their time.
Students compared them with modern metal and plastic pipes.
The old pipe made infrastructure visible. Usually, people think about water only when it stops running.
The visit showed that daily comfort depends on hidden systems built and repaired by many workers. A city is not only what stands above ground. It is also what quietly carries life below.
